feed.title: NPR Programs: All Things Considered
feed.subtitle: All Things Considered hosts Ailsa Chang, Mary Louise Kelly, Juana Summers and Scott Detrow present the program's trademark mix of news, interviews, commentaries, reviews, and offbeat features 7 days a week.

entry.title: U.S. Forest Service to keep some research stations open, after pushback about restructuring
entry.summary: In a massive restructuring under the Trump administration, U.S. Forest Service is closing dozens of research stations but, as NPR's Chiara Eisner reports, it is keeping some facilities open that had been projected to shutter.

entry.title: U.S. strikes three Iranian oil tankers in renewal of hostilities
entry.summary: The U.S. strikes three Iranian oil tankers after Iran targets two American warships, in the latest exchange over shipping and the Strait of Hormuz.

entry.title: I don't think I had $10 in the bank: Angela Davis remembers Gloria Steinem's allyship
entry.summary: Activist and author Angela Davis remembers her friend Gloria Steinem, and discusses intersectional feminism today.

entry.title: Jazz legend John Coltrane's Philadelphia house to become a cultural heritage site
entry.summary: On the centennial of father's birth, Ravi Coltrane talks about turning the home where the jazz legend spent a crucial period in the 1950s into a cultural heritage and community space.

entry.title: The Republican midterm convention is taking place in the heart of Bush country
entry.summary: The Republican midterm convention in Dallas takes place in the same city that helped give rise to the Bush political dynasty. Still, many policies championed by the conservative presidents are noticeably absent from today's Republican Party.

entry.title: This is the work of our lifetime: Ayana Elizabeth Johnson urges action after new UN climate report
entry.summary: A United Nations report has found that the world will warm to 1.5 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels. Climate solutions advocate Ayana Elizabeth Johnson urges a quicker implementation of known strategies - and determination rather than despair.

entry.title: Covering the wild world of prediction markets
entry.summary: NPR's Bobby Allyn talks about covering the prediction markets, where anyone can trade bets on the outcome of anything happening in the real world.

entry.title: Flock cameras draw opposition from across the political spectrum
entry.summary: As political races heat up heading into the midterms, candidates from both parties are increasingly joining the fray to voice concerns over Flock surveillance cameras.

entry.title: Musician Sara Bareilles talks about the importance of crying in her life
entry.summary: On Wild Card, famous guests answer questions that we don't always talk about. Musician Sara Bareilles talks about the importance of crying in her life.

entry.title: A stranger helped a mother and son stuck in a current in Lake Michigan
entry.summary: A mother was caught in a current while saving her son in Lake Michigan. When she couldn't get them closer to shore, a man appeared to help.
